content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson focuses on **Deployment and Scheduling**. Work through the listed subtopics (Running Pandas scripts outside notebooks, Using command-line parameters, Configuring input and output locations, Automating recurring reports) as decisions in one small data workflow: identify the input and its labels, choose the relevant Pandas operation, then inspect the output shape, values, and types. Do not assume the result is correct solely because the code ran.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Avoid assuming inferred types are always correct, treating every repeated record as an error, or overlooking alignment by labels. Check the actual API documentation for the target version and assert the properties that matter to the task.

task: Practise deployment and scheduling with a small synthetic DataFrame. Keep the input, transformation, and expected result explicit.
task_acceptance_criteria: The code uses an appropriate Pandas operation for the stated goal.
The result is checked for the expected values, labels, dtypes, row count, or alignment.
The solution documents a relevant edge case, assumption, or compatibility note.
hints: Start by printing the relevant shape, labels, and dtypes.
Write down the expected result for a tiny example before applying the operation to larger data.
Use a small assertion or comparison to verify the outcome instead of relying only on visual inspection.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting a result because the statement ran without raising an exception.
common_mistakes.why: A valid expression can still select the wrong rows, misalign labels, or use an unsuitable dtype.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the output shape, labels, dtypes, and at least one expected value.

common_mistakes.problem: Using the operation without considering missing values or duplicate keys.
common_mistakes.why: Those records may change totals, group sizes, or join cardinality.
common_mistakes.fix: State the policy and test an example containing the relevant edge case.

summary: Deployment and Scheduling supports one clearly defined part of a repeatable data workflow.
Check labels, dtypes, missing values, and row counts where they affect the result.
Record assumptions and consult the official reference when version-specific behavior matters.
